public_rationale: OpenAI's own o1 launch post compares o1 with GPT-4o. The largest gains it reports are on competition math. On AIME, GPT-4o solved about 12% of problems and o1 about 74%, roughly six times better. On GPQA Diamond the gain is about 1.4x, and on MMLU it is tiny. No metric OpenAI published comes anywhere near a hundredfold gain. Marcus's point that OpenAI's own data does not show o1 as 100 times better holds.
limitations: The baseline is GPT-4o, not the original GPT-4.
'Better' is undefined, so ratios of benchmark scores are only one reasonable measure.

from_speaker: is OpenAI's o1 100 times better than GPT4?
our_interpretation: Plain reading: none of OpenAI's own published o1 evaluations show anything close to a hundredfold gain over GPT-4-class models.
OpenAI's launch post compares o1 with GPT-4o, its GPT-4-family model at the time. I treat that as the 'GPT4' comparison OpenAI's own data offers.
The period is the state of OpenAI's published o1 data at the post date: from o1's announcement on 2024-09-12 to 2024-10-30.
criteria.support_condition: OpenAI's published o1 results show gains well below 100x over GPT-4/GPT-4o on its reported metrics.
criteria.contradiction_condition: An OpenAI-published metric shows o1 roughly 100 times better than GPT-4 or GPT-4o.

evidence.excerpt: GPT‑4o only solved on average 12% (1.8/15) of problems. o1 averaged 74% (11.1/15) with a single sample per problem
evidence.explanation: On AIME, one of OpenAI's best showcases for o1, the gain is about sixfold (74% vs 12%), far below 100x.
On GPQA Diamond, GPT-4o scored 56.1 and o1 78.0, a gain of about 1.4x. Other rows (MMLU 88.0 vs 90.8, MATH 60.3 vs 94.8) also show modest gains.
